title: Taylor Swift Makes Chart History with 4 Songs in the Top 10!
summary: Have you ever tried to get four of your favorite songs stuck in your head at once? Taylor Swift just did something even harder—she got four different songs into the top 10 of a big music chart all in the same week! It's a record no one else has ever broken, and it happened on the Adult Contemporary chart, which has been around since 1961. That's older than most parents! The song that pushed her over the top is called 'Elizabeth Taylor.' It jumped up to number 10, joining three other Swift songs already in the top 10: 'The Fate of Ophelia' at number 7, 'Opalite' at number 8, and 'I Knew It, I Knew You' at number 9. They're all lined up in a row, like ducks in a carnival game. Before this, the only time anyone had four songs in the top 10 at once was during the holidays, when Michael Bublé's Christmas album took over. But for regular, non-holiday weeks? Taylor is the first. 'I Knew It, I Knew You' is from the Toy Story 5 soundtrack—yes, that Toy Story!—and it already hit number 1 on the Hot 100 chart in June. 'Elizabeth Taylor' is her 23rd top 10 hit on this chart, more than any other singer since 2008. She also has nine number-one songs on this chart, starting with 'Love Story' way back in 2009. Taylor is also closing in on another record: she now has 29 top 10 hits on the Pop Airplay chart, just one behind Rihanna's record of 30. With all these songs climbing, it's clear Taylor Swift's music is still burning bright. As she sings in 'Elizabeth Taylor,' 'You're only as hot as your last hit, baby'—and right now, she's on fire!
why_it_matters: Taylor Swift's record shows that when you work hard at something you love, like making music, you can achieve things nobody has ever done before—just like practicing a sport or an instrument can help you break your own personal best.

background_read: Billboard, the music magazine that compiles all of these charts, has been ranking hits since the 1940s.
The Adult Contemporary chart (a list of songs that appeal to older listeners, not just teens) began in 1961, making it one of the oldest music charts still in use.
Taylor Swift started out as a country singer in Tennessee but has become a global pop phenomenon, breaking records across many different charts.
Article_Structure: WHAT: Placed four songs in the top 10 of the Adult Contemporary chart at the same time—a first in non-holiday weeks.
WHERE: On the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart, which ranks songs for adult listeners and has been around since 1961.
WHY: Her new songs, including 'Elizabeth Taylor' and a track from Toy Story 5, are getting lots of radio airplay and fan streaming.

perspectives.description: They celebrate her historic wins and see her as a role model who keeps pushing the boundaries of what's possible in music.
They might argue that having so many songs from one artist in the top 10 at once shows radio stations play too much of the same music, limiting variety.
They view this as a remarkable moment for the Adult Contemporary chart, which has tracked music for over 60 years, proving Taylor's lasting appeal across generations.
